import { test, expect } from 'claude-code/testing'

const TOOL = 'mcp__sonata-loop__sonata_loop'
const said = (r: { deny?: string; text?: string; result?: unknown }): string =>
  r.deny ?? r.text ?? (typeof r.result === 'string' ? r.result : '')

test('the tool validates and records the plan', async ($, on) => {
  on('ui.open', () => ({ value: { isPlaced: true } }))
  expect(said(await $.tool.call({ tool: TOOL, action: 'start', taskId: '1', phase: 'code' }))).toMatch(/call plan first/)
  expect(said(await $.tool.call({ tool: TOOL, action: 'plan', title: 't', tasks: [{ id: '1', title: 'A' }] }))).toMatch(/1 task/)
  expect(said(await $.tool.call({ tool: TOOL, action: 'start', taskId: '1', phase: 'code' }))).toMatch(/recorded/)
})

test('/clear empties the panel', async ($, on) => {
  on('ui.open', () => ({ value: { isPlaced: true } }))
  on('session.end', () => ({ sessionId: 's' }))
  await $.tool.call({ tool: TOOL, action: 'plan', title: 't', tasks: [{ id: '1', title: 'A' }] })
  await $.session.end({ reason: 'clear' })
  expect(said(await $.tool.call({ tool: TOOL, action: 'start', taskId: '1', phase: 'code' }))).toMatch(/call plan first/)
})

test('the tool answers with a string result, the shape the host accepts', async ($, on) => {
  on('ui.open', () => ({ value: { isPlaced: true } }))
  const r = await $.tool.call({ tool: TOOL, action: 'plan', title: 't', tasks: [{ id: '1', title: 'A' }] })
  expect(typeof (r as { result?: unknown }).result).toBe('string')
})

test('registers no command of its own: the panel rides on the skill\'s /sonata-loop', async ($, on) => {
  const names: string[] = []
  on('tool.register', () => ({ value: {} }))
  on('command.register', (_$, e) => { names.push((e as { name: string }).name); return { value: {} } })
  on('session.start', () => ({ cwd: '/tmp' }))
  await $.session.start({ source: 'startup', cwd: '/tmp' } as never)
  expect(names).toEqual([])
})

test('/sonata-loop panel toggles the pane and runs no skill', async ($, on) => {
  const opened: string[] = []
  let closed = 0
  let skillRuns = 0
  let panes: { id: string }[] = []
  on('ui.panes', () => ({ value: panes }))
  on('ui.open', (_$, e) => { opened.push((e as { id: string }).id); return { value: { isPlaced: true } } })
  on('ui.close', () => { closed++; return { value: {} } })
  on('command.run', () => { skillRuns++; return { text: 'skill ran' } })
  const run = (args: string) => $.command.run({ command: 'sonata-loop', args } as never)
  expect((await run('panel')).text).toBe('Loop panel opened.')
  expect(opened).toEqual(['sonata-loop'])
  panes = [{ id: 'sonata-loop' }]
  expect((await run(' Panel ')).text).toBe('Loop panel closed.')
  expect(closed).toBe(1)
  expect(skillRuns).toBe(0)
})

test('/sonata-loop with anything else runs the skill as typed', async ($, on) => {
  const seen: string[] = []
  on('command.run', (_$, e) => { seen.push((e as { args: string }).args); return { text: 'skill ran' } })
  expect((await $.command.run({ command: 'sonata-loop', args: 'add a logout button' } as never)).text).toBe('skill ran')
  expect((await $.command.run({ command: 'sonata-loop', args: '' } as never)).text).toBe('skill ran')
  expect(seen).toEqual(['add a logout button', ''])
})

test('an agent finishing triggers one more router fetch, so its last request is counted', async ($, on) => {
  let fetches = 0
  on('ui.open', () => ({ value: { isPlaced: true } }))
  on('agent.spawn', () => ({ model: 'sonata-code-simple', agentId: 'a1' }))
  on('session.id', () => ({ value: 's1' }))
  on('http.fetch', () => { fetches++; return { value: { status: 200, ok: true, headers: {}, text: '{"routes":[]}' } } })
  let parked!: () => void
  const isParked = new Promise<void>(r => { parked = r })
  on('clock.sleep', () => { parked(); return new Promise(() => {}) })
  on('turn.complete', () => ({ text: '' }))
  await $.agent.spawn({ subagentType: 'code-simple', description: 'x', prompt: 'x' } as never)
  await isParked
  const before = fetches
  await $.turn.complete({ agentId: 'a1', reason: 'answer', answer: '', durationMs: 1, isAborted: false, turnId: 't' } as never)
  expect(fetches).toBe(before + 1)
})
===== FILE 20 skills/loop/hooks/register.tsx =====
import { atom, read, update } from 'claude-code'
import type { EngineInterface, Register } from 'claude-code'
import type { AgentRow, Loop, RouterState, View } from '../types'
import { addHunks, addUsage, applyLoopAction, completeAgent, hunksFor, spawnAgent, stepAgent, toolActivity } from './model'
import { panelTree } from './panel'
import type { PanelActions, PanelData } from './panel'

const PLUGIN = 'sonata-loop'
const PANE = 'sonata-loop'

export const loopAtom = atom({ plugin: 'sonata-loop', key: 'loop' } as const, null as Loop | null)
export const agentsAtom = atom({ plugin: 'sonata-loop', key: 'agents' } as const, [] as AgentRow[])
export const routerAtom = atom({ plugin: 'sonata-loop', key: 'router' } as const, { routes: [] } as RouterState)
export const viewAtom = atom({ plugin: 'sonata-loop', key: 'view' } as const, { showAll: true, expanded: [] } as View)

const TOOL_DESCRIPTION = [
  'Report sonata-loop progress to the loop panel. Call it at each loop step:',
  'plan {title, tasks:[{id,title}]} after planning; start {taskId, phase: code|fix|review|final}',
  'right before each dispatch; result {taskId, outcome: pass|fail, note?} after each review;',
  'escalate {taskId, to: simple|normal|complex}; done {summary?} at the end.',
].join(' ')

// The keys tool.call carries beside a tool's own arguments.
const RESERVED = new Set(['tool', 'tool_use_id', 'agentId', 'consent', 'requestMeta'])
const argsOf = (e: object): Record<string, unknown> =>
  Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(e).filter(([k]) => !RESERVED.has(k)))

// Module state: reset on reload. A poll restarts on the next spawn or step, so
// a reload mid-loop does not freeze the model and cost columns.
let routerUrl = 'http://127.0.0.1:4100'
let polling = false
// The session's directory, so the panel can show diff paths relative to it.
let sessionCwd: string | undefined
// Marks router resets, so a fetch started before one cannot write stale state after it.
let epoch = 0

// One read of the router's view of this session.
async function fetchOnce($: EngineInterface): Promise<void> {
  const mine = epoch
  try {
    const session = await $.session.id()
    const res = await $.http.fetch(`${routerUrl}/__sonata/api/session/${encodeURIComponent(session)}`)
    if (!res.ok) {
      await update($, routerAtom, r => (mine === epoch ? { ...r, error: `router answered ${res.status}` } : r))
      return
    }
    let parsed: unknown
    try {
      parsed = JSON.parse(res.text)
    } catch {
      await update($, routerAtom, r => (mine === epoch ? { ...r, error: 'router answered with an unreadable body' } : r))
      return
    }
    const routes = (parsed as { routes?: unknown } | null | undefined)?.routes
    if (!Array.isArray(routes)) {
      await update($, routerAtom, r => (mine === epoch ? { ...r, error: 'router replied with no routes' } : r))
      return
    }
    // Only route-shaped entries: one `null`, or a `ts` Date.parse cannot read,
    // would crash every attribution and with it the pane.
    const optional = (v: unknown, kind: 'string' | 'number') =>
      v === undefined || (kind === 'number' ? typeof v === 'number' && Number.isFinite(v) : typeof v === kind)
    const kept = routes.filter((x): x is RouterState['routes'][number] => {
      if (typeof x !== 'object' || x === null) return false
      const r = x as Record<string, unknown>
      return typeof r.alias === 'string' && optional(r.ts, 'string') && optional(r.served, 'string')
        && optional(r.tier, 'string') && optional(r.priceUsd, 'number')
        && (r.isCovered === undefined || r.isCovered === true)
    })
    await update($, routerAtom, r => (mine === epoch ? { routes: kept, at: Date.now() } : r))
  } catch {
    await update($, routerAtom, r => (mine === epoch ? { ...r, error: 'router not reachable' } : r))
  }
}

// Polls while any agent runs; stops by itself, and runs one at a time.
async function poll($: EngineInterface): Promise<void> {
  if (polling) return
  polling = true
  try {
    while ((await read($, agentsAtom)).some(a => a.status === 'running')) {
      await fetchOnce($)
      await $.clock.sleep(3_000)
    }
  } catch {
    // The poll is started unawaited (`void poll($)`). An engine call it is
    // waiting on can be rejected when the environment goes away (a reload,
    // a torn-down test); that ends this poll, and the next spawn or step
    // starts another. It must never surface as an unhandled rejection.
  } finally {
    polling = false
  }
}

export const register: Register = (on, options) => {
  routerUrl = String((options as { router_url?: unknown } | undefined)?.router_url ?? 'http://127.0.0.1:4100')
  on('session.start', async ($, e, next) => {
    await $.tool.register({
      name: 'sonata_loop',
      description: TOOL_DESCRIPTION,
      isDeferred: false,
      inputSchema: {
        type: 'object',
        properties: {
          action: { enum: ['plan', 'start', 'result', 'escalate', 'done'] },
          title: { type: 'string' }, taskId: { type: 'string' }, summary: { type: 'string' }, note: { type: 'string' },
          phase: { enum: ['code', 'fix', 'review', 'final'] }, outcome: { enum: ['pass', 'fail'] },
          to: { enum: ['simple', 'normal', 'complex'] },
          tasks: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: { id: { type: 'string' }, title: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['id', 'title'] } },
        },
        required: ['action'],
      },
    })
    const started = await next(e)
    sessionCwd = started.cwd
    return started
  })

  on('session.end', async ($, e, next) => {
    if (e.reason === 'clear') {
      await update($, loopAtom, () => null)
      await update($, agentsAtom, () => [])
      await update($, viewAtom, () => ({ showAll: true, expanded: [] }))
      epoch++
      await update($, routerAtom, () => ({ routes: [] }))
    }
    return next(e)
  })

  // One command: `/sonata-loop panel` toggles the pane; anything else is the
  // skill's own /sonata-loop, passed on untouched.
  on('command.run', { command: 'sonata-loop' }, async ($, e, next) => {
    if (e.args.trim().toLowerCase() !== 'panel') return next(e)
    const isOpen = (await $.ui.panes()).some(p => p.id === PANE)
    if (isOpen) await $.ui.close({ id: PANE })
    else await $.ui.open({ id: PANE, title: 'sonata loop' })
    return { text: isOpen ? 'Loop panel closed.' : 'Loop panel opened.' }
  })

  // The mod's own tool: the one place a refusal is allowed (validation only).
  on('tool.call', { tool: 'mcp__sonata-loop__sonata_loop' }, async ($, e) => {
    const input = argsOf(e)
    const result = applyLoopAction(await read($, loopAtom), input, Date.now())
    if ('error' in result) return { deny: result.error }
    await update($, loopAtom, () => result.loop)
    if (input.action === 'plan') {
      // A new loop replaces the last one's rows, so they cannot linger or blur attribution.
      await update($, agentsAtom, () => [])
      epoch++
      await update($, routerAtom, () => ({ routes: [] }))
      await update($, viewAtom, () => ({ showAll: true, expanded: [] }))
      void $.ui.open({ id: PANE, title: 'sonata loop' })
    }
    const n = result.loop?.tasks.length ?? 0
    // A registered tool's result is a string (or content blocks), never an object.
    return { result: `sonata_loop recorded (${n} task${n === 1 ? '' : 's'}).` }
  })

  on('agent.spawn', async ($, e, next) => {
    const started = await next(e)
    if ('agentId' in started && started.agentId !== undefined) {
      const s = spawnAgent(
        { loop: await read($, loopAtom), agents: await read($, agentsAtom) },
        { agentId: started.agentId, subagentType: e.subagentType, description: e.description, parentAgentId: e.parentAgentId },
        Date.now(),
      )
      await update($, loopAtom, () => s.loop)
      await update($, agentsAtom, () => s.agents)
      void poll($)
    }
    return started
  })

  on('turn.step', async function* ($, e, next) {
    if (e.agentId !== undefined) {
      const agentId = e.agentId
      await update($, agentsAtom, a => stepAgent(a, { agentId, model: e.model }, Date.now()))
      void poll($)
    }
    const result = yield* next(e)
    // The engine's own count of what this step's request moved: no router needed.
    if (e.agentId !== undefined && result?.usage) {
      const agentId = e.agentId
      const usage = result.usage
      await update($, agentsAtom, a => addUsage(a, agentId, usage))
    }
    return result
  })

  // Every other tool call: observe the subagent's activity and its applied edits.
  on('tool.call', async ($, e, next) => {
    const agentId = e.agentId
    const input = argsOf(e)
    if (agentId !== undefined) await update($, agentsAtom, a => toolActivity(a, { agentId, tool: e.tool, input }))
    const ran = await next(e)
    if (agentId !== undefined && !('deny' in ran && ran.deny !== undefined) && ran.isError !== true) {
      const hunks = hunksFor(e.tool, input)
      if (hunks.length > 0) await update($, agentsAtom, a => addHunks(a, agentId, hunks))
    }
    return ran
  })

  on('turn.complete', async ($, e, next) => {
    if (e.agentId !== undefined) {
      const agentId = e.agentId
      await update($, agentsAtom, a => completeAgent(a, { agentId, reason: e.reason }, Date.now()))
      // The poll may stop before the router logs this agent's last request.
      await fetchOnce($)
    }
    return next(e)
  })

  // $ never crosses an import, so the hook gathers the data and the press
  // handlers here and panel.tsx only arranges them.
  on('ui.render', { component: 'Pane', requestId: PANE }, async ($, e) => {
    const data: PanelData = {
      loop: await read($, loopAtom),
      agents: await read($, agentsAtom),
      router: await read($, routerAtom),
      view: await read($, viewAtom),
      now: Date.now(),
      cwd: sessionCwd,
      cols: Number((e as { props?: { bodyColumns?: unknown } }).props?.bodyColumns) || 80,
    }
    const act: PanelActions = {
      select: key => void update($, viewAtom, v => ({ ...v, selected: v.selected === key ? undefined : key })),
      toggleFold: key => void update($, viewAtom, v => ({
        ...v, expanded: v.expanded.includes(key) ? v.expanded.filter(k => k !== key) : [...v.expanded, key],
      })),
      toggleActive: () => void update($, viewAtom, v => ({ ...v, showAll: !v.showAll })),
      jumpLatest: () => void $.ui.scroll({ in: PANE, to: 'end' }),
      copy: text => void $.ui.copy({ text }),
    }
    return panelTree(h, $.ui.resolve(e), data, act)
  })
}
===== FILE 21 skills/loop/types/index.d.ts =====
export type Tier = 'simple' | 'normal' | 'complex'
export type Phase = 'code' | 'fix' | 'review' | 'final'
export type TaskState = 'pending' | 'coding' | 'fixing' | 'review' | 'done'

export type LoopTask = {
  id: string
  title: string
  state: TaskState
  failures: number
  escalatedTo?: Tier
  /** The phase of the last `start`, until its `result`. */
  openPhase?: Phase
  agentIds: string[]
}

export type Loop = {
  title: string
  tasks: LoopTask[]
  /** Set by `start`; the next top-level sonata spawn attaches here. */
  pendingTaskId?: string
  isDone: boolean
  summary?: string
  startedAt: number
}

export type AgentStatus = 'running' | 'done' | 'aborted' | 'error'

export type Hunk = {
  file: string
  removed: string[]
  added: string[]
  /** Lines cut by the 40-line cap. */
  omitted: number
  isNewFile: boolean
}

export type AgentRow = {
  id: string
  type: string
  description: string
  parentId?: string
  taskId?: string
  status: AgentStatus
  activity?: string
  steps: number
  /** The model alias its requests name (`sonata-code-auto`). */
  alias?: string
  /** Epoch ms of each `turn.step`, for matching router routes. */
  stepTimes: number[]
  usedBash: boolean
  /** Summed from each step's reported usage; absent until one reports. */
  tokens?: { input: number; output: number; cacheRead: number; cacheWrite: number }
  hunks: Hunk[]
  startedAt: number
  endedAt?: number
}

export type RouteLine = {
  alias: string
  served?: string
  status: number
  ts?: string
  role?: string
  tier?: string
  priceUsd?: number
  isCovered?: true
}

export type RouterState = {
  routes: RouteLine[]
  error?: string
  /** When the router was last read successfully (epoch ms). */
  at?: number
}

export type View = { selected?: string; showAll: boolean; expanded: string[] }

declare module 'claude-code' {
  interface PluginState {
    'sonata-loop': {
      loop: Loop | null
      agents: AgentRow[]
      router: RouterState
      view: View
    }
  }
}

<!--
Closing keywords are how an issue closes itself. GitHub closes an issue when a
merged PR's *description* says `Closes #n` / `Fixes #n` / `Resolves #n` — a
bare `#n` only links, which is how #41 stayed open through the PR that fixed
it. Squash merges honour this the same way.

Reference a pull request as `PR #n`, never a bare `#n`: CodeRabbit's
out-of-scope check reads a bare number as a linked *issue* and then correctly
reports that this PR does not implement it. That warning on #48 was caused by
the description, not the code.

Delete whichever lines below do not apply — an empty heading is worse than no
heading.
-->

## What changed

## Why

# Generated per-user by `sonata init` (contains absolute paths)
.mcp.json
sonata.toml

# Everything under .claude/ is per-machine, not source: agents and skills that
# `sonata init`/`sonata sync` generate from this machine's sonata.toml, and the
# routing state `sonata route` writes into settings. Ignored wholesale so a new
# file Claude Code or sonata starts writing there does not silently become a
# candidate for commit.
.claude/

# Isolated worktrees for subagent-driven plan execution (git-ignored scratch).
.worktrees/

# Impeccable's session scratch: the decision-page payloads/answers and the
# detector's cache are per-run, not source. The surface briefs under
# .impeccable/surfaces/ ARE source — they carry each surface's direction
# contract, which later sessions reload — so they are force-added below.
.impeccable/questions/
.impeccable/hook.cache.json

# The docs site's build output and VitePress's dev cache (docs/.vitepress/dist
# is already covered by `dist/` above).
docs/.vitepress/cache/

# local runtime state: config, keys, usage ledger, litellm venv (never commit)
/state/

# Surface brief — sonata's terminal interface

**Scope:** `src/tui-ink/` — the Ink surfaces of `sonata init`, `sonata agents`,
`sonata status` / `doctor`, and `sonata tui`. All four are co-equal.

**Visitor mode:** Operate. Someone mid-task, in tmux or over SSH, completing a
task or finding out why one failed.

**Audience and job:** developers running Claude Code who want a subagent on a
foreign model. Built for its author, but strangers are the goal — someone who
found the package on npm and must reach a working routed agent alone.

**Constraints that bind every screen:** own the ground and the foreground as
an explicit pair (reversed 2026-09-23 from "never own the background", which
made a light theme impossible — see PRODUCT.md); degrade to 16 colours and
keyboard only; readable in a split pane; never block in a hook. Colour is
never the sole carrier of meaning.

**Unresolved:** whether `sonata tui`'s dashboard shares the board grammar or
earns a second composition. Decide when that surface is built, not before.

## Direction contract

**THESIS.** A tier is a departure board: one service goes, the rest stand by in
declared order. The screen's job is to show the whole chain — what is running,
what follows it, what is delayed and why — not merely the current selection. It
refuses the category default, a titled checkbox list over a dim hint line,
which shows the cursor and hides the consequence. What sonata ranks is
fallback depth, and depth is the one thing a checkbox list cannot draw.

**OWN-WORLD.** Rows on a shared baseline under a fixed head, each carrying a
service number, a name, a measured quantity, and a status held in its own
right-hand column. State is stroke, not hue: live reads unbroken, cooled as a
clean gap, dominated as an open ring, pinned as doubled — so the board survives
monochrome, and colour only ever reinforces. One warm accent marks the lead
service and the committing key, never decoration. Everything else is graphite
and the terminal's own foreground. Quantities are bars against a scale shared
across rows, because the question is always comparative. Rules are hairline and
rare: one under the head, one above provenance. Nothing disappears — a cooled
gateway and a dominated model stay on the board, struck.

**STORY.** The reader arrives knowing a role and a difficulty, not a model.
They see which service leads and what it costs, that others stand behind it in
order, and that a delay is a stated condition with a time, not an error. They
leave having set an ordering they can read back, understanding that choosing
the tier was choosing the model.

**FIRST VIEWPORT.** `sonata init`'s ranking screen at 96×24. Head line: role
and tier left, count chosen right. A hairline rule. Then the board: rank
numeral in accent, model and effort, a capability bar on the shared scale, cost
right-aligned and decimal-aligned, status last. The lead service sits above a
rule, apart from standby rows. Dominated candidates render struck beneath.
Second hairline, then provenance — the catalog and its date. The keymap is the
last line, key then action, double-space separated, never middle-dot prose.
The committing key is the only other accent on screen.

**FORM.** The Departure Board (solari split-flap boards), position 1 of 7 on
the ordered grounded list, chosen by the user over the assigned roll. Seed key
`afb4e0bc`; resolved as kind `pick`. Signature interaction: re-ranking moves a
row and its whole service — numeral, bar and status travel together, so the
board is always readable as an order rather than as markers that swap. Motion
is one orchestrated line-settle on reorder; nothing else animates, and no
split-flap is imitated because a terminal cannot do it honestly.

**FINISH.** unreviewed and undocumented is unfinished; this build ends with the
finish review, the verdict, DESIGN.md, and every shipping raster carrying its
provenance

===== FILE 30 CHANGELOG.md =====
# Changelog

All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.

The format follows [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project uses [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/) informally
(pre-1.0, so minor bumps can carry breaking changes).

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- **Dashboard username + password login.** `sonata dashboard set-password
  [--user <name>] [--random]` stores a scrypt-hashed account in
  `~/.config/sonata/ui-users.json` (0600, atomic write; password read from stdin
  with no echo on a terminal, at least 12 characters, `--random` prints a
  generated one once). `POST /__sonata/api/login` (JSON only, same-origin,
  at most 4 KiB, constant-time verify with a dummy verify for unknown users)
  opens the same `sonata_ui` session the `?k=` link does; `POST
  /__sonata/api/logout` ends it. They are the only routes exempt from the
  session/CSRF requirement. An in-memory limiter slows guessing with
  progressive waits instead of lockouts: the Nth consecutive failure for a
  username within 15 minutes makes its next attempt wait min(2^(N-1), 30) s
  (attempts during the wait get `429` + `Retry-After` unverified and do not
  extend it), and the global failure count adds the same scheme capped at 5 s,
  so nobody can lock the owner out; it never trusts `X-Forwarded-For`. A
  password session is bound to its account and credential: `sonata dashboard
  set-password` or removing the account ends it (`?k=` sessions are
  unchanged). The dashboard shows a sign-in screen when the router
  refuses its reads, falls back to it when a session disappears, and has a
  Sign out button in the sidebar. The `?k=` link login is unchanged.

### Security

- **The proxy surface now answers to a loopback Host only (fail-closed).** The
  Host gate used to refuse only names listed in `[ui] allowed_hosts`, so an
  unlisted, malformed, comma-joined or missing Host still reached `/v1/*` and
  `/__sonata_health` — a DNS-rebinding page could drive the proxy with the
  stored gateway keys. Every path other than `/` and `/__sonata/*` now needs
  `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or `[::1]` (with the router's port or none) and is
  otherwise answered 403 without echoing anything, whether or not
  `allowed_hosts` is configured. The dashboard keeps its own rule (loopback or
  an exact `allowed_hosts` name). `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:<port>`
  and the `localhost` health probe are unaffected; a client that reaches the
  router under another name must use a loopback one.
- **Dashboard write path tightened.** `alerts.command` and `ui.allowed_hosts`
  are refused from the dashboard (403) and stay settable with `sonata config
  set`. A request under a `[ui] allowed_hosts` name now needs a session cookie
  for every `/__sonata/api/*` read and is refused (403) for any path outside `/`
  and `/__sonata/*`, so the proxy surface is not reachable through that name.
  `?%6B=` (an encoded `k`) is stripped from proxied urls like `?k=`. An unknown
  API path's 404 no longer echoes the path.

### Fixed

- `/__sonata_health` and the dashboard no longer re-parse every tenant config
  and the multi-megabyte models.dev catalog on each call to list tenants: the
  tenant summary now needs only ids and paths (about 77 ms down to 0.4 ms per
  call on a real state directory). The ledger snapshot's covered window has 10 s
  of slack, so a `now - 30d` read computed just before a refresh stays in memory,
  and its warm-up now starts before the router waits for LiteLLM.
- Dashboard tier reorders work when a tier has disabled candidates (the disabled
  entries keep their positions), keep a collapsed role collapsed, and the
  settings write no longer blocks the router's event loop while waiting for the
  config lock. The budget field rejects zero, matching the router.

### Changed

- **`sonata restart` no longer interrupts a request in flight.** The router is
  never idle (every Claude Code session on the machine goes through it), and a
  restart used to kill it with whatever streams it was answering. Now the new
  router is started first and waits at the port; only when it reports ready is
  the old router told to drain (SIGUSR2, which `restart` records support for in
  the serve state). The old listener closes at once, idle keep-alive sockets are
  closed, every request being answered runs to completion, and the process exits
  afterwards, capped at 15 minutes. Measured against real processes: a 12-chunk
  stream survived a restart, new requests landed on the new router, and the
  longest gap in a 10 ms probe loop was 70 ms (one refused connection in 756).
  A successor that cannot start (bad config, crash) never costs the old router
  its port: the restart fails and the old router carries on (and the detached
  successor is stopped). Only SIGUSR2, which `restart` sends, drains; SIGTERM,
  SIGINT and SIGHUP stop at once exactly as before, and a second signal cuts a
  drain short. The SIGUSR2 handler is installed before the router binds, and the
  router writes `handoff: true` to its state only once it exists — SIGUSR2's
  default action would end a half-started router and orphan its LiteLLM; one
  that arrives mid-start now waits for the router to be up and then drains. The
  stopping signals are handled from the start too: SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP
  during start-up stop the LiteLLM already spawned, clear the state record and
  remove the temp directory before the process ends, instead of the default
  action leaving all three behind. A
  draining router writes `draining: true` to its state entry.
- **A running LiteLLM survives a restart when nothing it was started for
  changed.** The router records the LiteLLM it started — pid, port, master key,
  directory, the plan snapshot it was started for, and the ChatGPT login it was
  seeded with — and the router that replaces it adopts it when the pid is
  positively a LiteLLM, answers with the recorded key, and the successor's own
  plan snapshot matches. LiteLLM now writes to a log file beside its config
  (followed by the router) rather than to a pipe, which would kill it with the
  router it was spawned by. When the plan differs, the successor starts its own
  LiteLLM on the next free port while the old router keeps the old one for its
  in-flight requests; each router stops only the LiteLLM it owns, and the state
  file lists a replaced router and its LiteLLM so a router that dies mid-drain
  cannot orphan it unnoticed; entries are swept (child stopped, directory
  removed) before they are forgotten. LiteLLM's log is capped at 20 MB (copied
  to `.1` and truncated in place, checked after every read so continuous
  output rotates too), each temp directory carries an `owner.pid`,
  and a starting router — including one with no earlier state — removes
  `sonata-litellm-*` directories whose owner is gone. `/__sonata_health` reports the LiteLLM port in use and `sonata doctor`
  probes that port; the pid-reuse guards read `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` by default
  (they were unwired for an adopted child). Each restart's standby marker is
  per successor pid.
- **`sonata restart` refuses to replace a router started from a different
  install** (a development build, a worktree, a test copy) and names both
  paths; `--force` overrides. The router's install is the real path of the
  `cli.js` in its `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` (a relative path is resolved against
  the router's own `/proc/<pid>/cwd`); where that cannot be read, nothing is
  refused.

### Added

- **Terminal: verdict line, `why`, `config get|set`, `enable|disable`.**
  `sonata status`, `usage` and `limits` now open with the console's one-line
  verdict (`buildVerdict`, coloured by level on a terminal), and `status` and
  `usage` follow it with each Go account's 5 h / week / month bars (`bar`,
  `barValues` from `console/explain.ts`; `limits` uses the same `bar`). `--json`
  gains an additive `verdict` field on `limits` and `usage`. `sonata why
  [request-id|last]` prints the explain text of one request (exit 1 for an
  unknown id), through the same `explainPayload` as the dashboard route.
  `sonata config get <dotted.path>` / `set <dotted.path> <value>` run
  `getSetting` / `setSetting`, printing the validator's message and exiting 1 on
  a refusal. `sonata enable|disable <gateway|model>` resolves a name or a short
  form (`ucha1`, `primary`; ambiguous names are listed and nothing changes),
  flips the same `enabled` flag Settings does, and prints which tier lists
  lose or gain a candidate.

- **Inside Claude Code — `sonata statusline` and `/sonata*` slash commands.**
  `sonata statusline [--color]` prints one short segment for a status line
  script: `sonata: ok`, `sonata: backup (ucha1 14%)` (a Go account is capped and
  the named one serves, with its 5h usage), `sonata: degraded`, or
  `sonata: down` (every Go account capped, nothing else reachable). The level
  comes from `buildVerdict` over `computeLimits` and the ladders, so it agrees
  with `sonata limits` and the dashboard. No network; it reads a week of ledger
  (the span the cap scan needs), caches the answer for 10 s, serves a stale
  answer (up to 2 min old) while a detached child recomputes it, and prints
  nothing with exit 0 on any failure. `sonata-statusline` (a second bin) is the
  same command without loading the whole CLI first, about 40 ms on a cache hit
  against ~400 ms for `sonata statusline`. `sonata sync` now also writes
  `/sonata`, `/sonata-why`, `/sonata-accounts` and `/sonata-limits` into
  `.claude/commands` beside the agents: each runs the CLI through `!`-bash and
  asks Claude to summarize. Only files carrying sonata's marker are created or
  updated; a same-named file of the user's is skipped and reported, nothing is
  ever deleted by `sync`, and `sonata reset` removes only the marked ones.

- **`sonata top` — a live terminal screen.** A btop-style Ink screen that
  refreshes every 2 s and fits 80x24: the verdict line (coloured by level),
  each OpenCode Go account's 5h / week / month bars with its capped flag and
  frees-up time, the busiest ladder's candidates as green / yellow / red /
  grey chips (with a marker where the router skips a candidate), the running
  runs, and the newest ledger calls. Keys: `q` quit, `a` accounts focus, `l`
  cycle ladders, `r` runs focus, up/down select a call, `e` explain the
  selected (else newest) call, `s` the `sonata config` / `enable` / `disable`
  commands. Everything is computed in-process from the same functions the
  dashboard uses (`buildVerdict`, `computeLimits`, `ladderStateFrom`,
  `explainRequest`, the run reader); when a router is running its own
  ladders are asked for in the background (every 30 s) so cooldowns show, and
  without one every other panel still works with cooldowns empty. Piped, it
  prints one plain-text snapshot and exits 0.

- **Router: a spent allowance, an account setting or a conversation shape no
  longer ends the ladder.** A `GoUsageLimitError` 429 from an OpenCode Go
  endpoint now cools the whole gateway for the length of the cap it names
  (`5h` 30 min, `weekly` 6 h, `monthly` 12 h, unknown 30 min) instead of 60 s,
  so a capped account is no longer retried on every rung; one probe request is
  let through once a quarter of the cooldown has passed (then at most every 10
  min), clearing it if served. A 400 naming an
  account setting (`trains on request data`, `requires Global regions`) falls
  past to the next candidate and cools that candidate for 60 min, on Go routes
  only. A 529 caused by cooling candidates now names each with its reason. A
  conversation-shape 400 (`No tool output found for function call`) falls past
  with no cooldown, for at most 4 candidates per request (it moved out of the capability list, which returned it
  twice and cooled on the third). Every other 400 is still terminal. The fall-pasts are
  recorded in the ledger as before; the 400 ones also store the refusal's
  message on the attempt (`attempt.error`), which the console's events, ladder
  chips and `explain` read. Long ladder cooldowns now read `cooling 6 h` /
  `cooling 30 min` instead of thousands of seconds.
- **Router: a reached daily budget keeps covered candidates serving.** On a tier
  request, `[budget] daily_usd` being reached now skips priced candidates and
  continues down the ladder with subscription, plan or explicit-$0 candidates,
  refusing with the usual message only when none remain. `-auto` tiers skip the
  classifier while over budget. An unreadable cap and non-tier requests still
  refuse outright.

- The router's dashboard is now a React + Vite app (`ui/`, built into `dist/ui/` by `npm run build`): Home, Console, Feed, Runs, Explain and Settings views, four palettes with glass and light/dark, Ctrl-K palette, bundled fonts and icons. The router serves the built assets with correct types, immutable caching for hashed files and no path traversal. The page still gets the write API's `sonata-csrf` meta only for a request holding a dashboard session, and every UI response (page, missing-build 503, JSON, assets) carries the frame-denial headers.

- **Dashboard read API — catalog, runs, and one aggregate refresh.** Three
  read-only routes complete the console's data half, all under the existing
  loopback guard. `GET /__sonata/api/catalog` lists every model any tier lists,
  once, with its gateway and shortened account, the effort levels the tiers
  pin, `enabled` from the gateway/model flags, the OpenCode Go list price per
  Mtok in/out, the context window (models.dev where it publishes one, else the
  config), and the Artificial Analysis numbers where a cache exists — per
  model and per effort level. A model with no price or no score answers `null`
  rather than a made-up zero. `GET /__sonata/api/runs` and `/api/runs/:id` read
  the run store through the same bounded reader the feed uses, so a run cannot
  be finished in one view and running in the other: state, role, tier alias
  where the config makes it unambiguous, and elapsed from the store's own
  stamps. The detail adds the account that served a routed run (one bounded
  ledger join on the run id), the last 40 lines of that run's log, redacted
  with the ledger's own sanitiser, plus the report (same credential redaction,
  keeping its line structure); a harness run's account is
  `null` rather than a guess, and ids are validated with `isRunId` before any
  path exists and a 404 never echoes one. `GET /__sonata/api/console` answers
  the dashboard home in one request — verdict, limits, ladders, the newest 20 feed events and the
  running plus newest 10 runs — built by calling those same payload functions;
  a part that throws answers `null` and names itself in `errors` while the
  response stays 200.
- **`[ui] allowed_hosts` now reaches the Host check.** A request whose Host
  header (lowercase, port stripped) exactly matches a listed host passes, so a
  reverse proxy in front of the router can serve the console; loopback stays
  allowed and an empty list is exactly the old loopback-only rule. No
  wildcards, and the config is re-read per request through a short cache, so a
  Settings edit takes effect without a restart. The loopback comparison is now
  case-insensitive too, so the two rules agree about the same header.
- **Console settings — `[alerts]`, `[ui] allowed_hosts`, gateway/model
  `enabled`, and a safe `sonata.toml` writer.** `[alerts]` carries `enabled`
  (default off), `command` (argv, message on stdin), per-event toggles
  (`account_capped`, `account_recovered`, `all_accounts_capped`,
  `model_blocked`, `budget_reached`, default on), an optional `daily_digest`
  time and `min_interval_minutes` (default 30); `[ui]` carries
  `allowed_hosts` (default empty, loopback stays the rule until the Host
  check lands). A native gateway or model with `enabled = false` drops out
  of every tier's candidate list at resolution time, and a tier left with no
  candidates is refused at load the way an empty tier is. `sonata init`
  carries all of these through a rewrite. `getSetting` / `setSetting` /
  `setSettings` (`src/console/settings.ts`) edit the machine file through
  the shared lock, validate with the same parser the router uses (leaving
  the file untouched on error), keep 10 timestamped backups, write temp +
  fsync + atomic rename through symlinks, and only accept an allow-list of
  paths (`alerts.*`, `ui.allowed_hosts`, gateway `enabled`/`plan`, model
  `enabled`, tier reorder as a permutation, `budget.daily_usd`). `enabled =
  false` removes a gateway or model from tier ladders; an explicit `--model`
  request still reaches it. All three `sonata.toml` writers (`init`, `agents`,
  settings) plus the TUI budget screen now take the same resolved-path session
  lock, so concurrent writes serialize instead of silently reverting one
  another. No CLI or
  dashboard route calls it yet. `reloadRunning` is a status check only: the
  serve daemon re-reads configs per request, so no restart is needed.
- **Verdict + explain — one plain sentence and per-request text for the
  console.** `buildVerdict` (`src/console/explain.ts`) answers `ok` /
  `degraded` / `down` in one sentence over the same limits + ladder state the
  Home view draws ("primary hit its weekly cap (frees ~Sun 14:00), ucha1
  serving at 14%"); `barValues` + `bar` give 0..1 CLI/UI bars per account
  window; `explainRequest` turns one ledger row into plain lines ("primary
  spark rejected: weekly cap", "answered in 31 s, 18.6k in / 1.2k out"),
  reusing the feed's wording helpers so no surface invents its own phrasing.
  Served as `GET /__sonata/api/verdict` and `GET /__sonata/api/explain/:id`
  (`last` = newest row, bounded read, 404 for unknown ids, no keys or bodies).
- **`sonata limits` — how much of each OpenCode Go account's allowance is
  used.** One line per Go gateway (any native gateway whose `base_url` is an
  OpenCode Go endpoint) showing the 5-hour, weekly and monthly windows as
  percentages of their caps, the week's top contributing models, and when each
  window is estimated to free up; `--json` returns the same report. The numbers
  come from sonata's own ledger valued at OpenCode's list prices, so they are
  **estimates**, and the windows are assumed rolling — the provider documents
  neither. Free models never count, and a model this build does not price is
  skipped rather than counted as $0. An account whose newest Go outcome is a
  usage-limit 429 (looking back a week, until a later success) is reported as
  `● capped (weekly)`, named from our own
  window arithmetic. Also served at `GET /__sonata/api/limits` for the local
  UI. See [docs/opencode-go-limits.md](docs/opencode-go-limits.md).
- **`plan = "go" | "go-plus"` on a native gateway** says which OpenCode Go
  plan an account is on; unset defaults to `go`, the smaller allowance. Refused
  on OAuth and session gateways, which have no such allowance, and carried
  through a `sonata init` rewrite like `billing`.
- **Live ladder state — one function every surface draws a tier's chips from.**
  `ladderState` (`src/console/ladders.ts`) answers, per `sonata-<role>-<tier>`
  alias, its candidates **in config rank order** and what the router would do
  with each: `serving`, `cooling`, `capped`, `blocked`, `idle` or
  `not_reached`, with a plain-words `reason` (`weekly cap`, `cooling 42 s`,
  `needs Global regions`). Caps and privacy blocks reuse the existing
  go-limits scan and `blockedSignature`, so this view cannot disagree with
  `sonata limits` or the console feed; cooldowns are the router's own live
  maps, read through a new read-only `cooldownsForTenant` accessor that returns
  copies. Served as `GET /__sonata/api/ladders` for the local UI.

### Fixed

- **The router no longer re-reads the ledger per request.** `sonata serve`
  pegged a core and took 25-55 s to answer `/__sonata_health` on a busy
  machine: with `[budget] daily_usd` set, every routed request re-read and
  re-parsed today's whole ledger file (8-21 MB), twice, plus the machine
  config twice; and every console endpoint did its own 30-day read (~55 MB,
  ~90k rows). A shared in-process snapshot (`src/ledger-snapshot.ts`) now
  holds the retention window once, advances it by reading only appended
  bytes (at most every 5 s, one refresh shared by concurrent callers; a row
  the router wrote itself is visible at once), and keeps the per-UTC-day
  priced totals, so the budget check is a lookup with no file I/O. Until the
  snapshot has loaded, the budget uses the old direct read, never zero.
  The machine config the budget needs is parsed once per change of
  `sonata.toml` (and the catalog caches it depends on). `/console`,
  `/limits`, `/ladders` and `/verdict` reuse a computed answer for 5 s,
  dropped sooner when the ledger moves or a settings write lands. The limits
  tile and the verdict share one limits computation per `/console` call.
  CLI commands still read the files directly.

## [0.16.6] - 2026-10-16

### Breaking

- **A `base_url` that carries an authority-confusion shape is refused at load.**
  This applies to `[native.gateways]` and `[auto_route]` `base_url`. Refused
  forms: userinfo (`https://user:pw@host`, `https://host@other`); a backslash
  anywhere (`https://openrouter.ai\@evil.example`); an `@` anywhere; a `%` in
  the host (`https://evil%2Eexample`); a query string or fragment (`?` or `#`);
  whitespace or a control character inside the URL; a scheme other than http or
  https; and a string that does not parse as a URL. These are refused because
  two URL parsers, Node's and the one LiteLLM's HTTP client uses, read the host
  of such a string differently, so a repo could pass the host check while its
  key went elsewhere. **Remedy:** write the plain URL, a scheme, a host, an
  optional port and a path. `https://openrouter.ai\@evil.example/api/v1` becomes
  `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1`; `https://host/v1?x=1` becomes `https://host/v1`;
  `https://user:pw@host` becomes `https://host`. Everything else is accepted and
  normalised: an uppercase scheme, an underscore host such as
  `http://ollama_server:11434`, an IDN host, a default port and surrounding
  whitespace.
- **A gateway may not be named `seeded`, the empty string, or a JavaScript object
  property name such as `constructor`, `toString` or `__proto__`.** Any other name,
  spaces included, is accepted. **Remedy:** rename the gateway. A name with a
  space now maps to a key variable of underscores (`SONATA_KEY_BAD_NAME` for
  `bad name`), so a rename changes nothing else.

### Security

- **A refused key host no longer tells the model how to trust it.** The router's
  error for a gateway whose host is not trusted for its key names the config
  file and points the user at `sonata doctor`; the runnable `sonata auth trust`
  command stays in serve's log and in `sonata doctor`, with the gateway and host
  shell-quoted. `sonata auth trust` now needs an interactive terminal and a typed
  `y`/`yes` (default no); it refuses when stdin is not a TTY. It also runs the
  upgrade seed first, as `auth untrust` does, so trusting one host first no longer
  forfeits the seed for the others.
- **Plain-http gateways off loopback are told to use https.** A keyed
  `http://192.168.1.5:8000/v1` (or an `[auto_route]` URL like it) can never be
  bound, so the message now says https is required and suggests no trust, and
  `sonata auth trust` refuses that host rather than reporting a binding that
  changes nothing.
- A rejected `base_url` no longer echoes its userinfo or query into the error.

- **A stored key is now sent only to a host bound to its gateway name.**
  Keys are looked up by gateway name, but the `base_url` they are sent to
  comes from a config — including a cloned repo's project config pointing the
  name at an attacker's host — so the name alone no longer decides where a key
  goes. A host is bound when it is the provider's own endpoint, you confirmed
  it with the new `sonata auth trust <gateway> <host>` (`untrust` removes it,
  `trust-list` lists), or it is the machine config's own URL for that name;
  `sonata auth add` and `sonata init` record the binding for the URL you
  chose. Anything else gets no key: `sonata serve` withholds it and answers a
  named 502 with the exact trust command, and `sonata doctor` fails the
  gateway the same way. Hostnames compare exactly (never suffix-matched),
  https only, except a loopback http host (`localhost`, `127.0.0.0/8`, `::1`).
  That is bound by the machine config's own URL (trusted by definition), by the
  upgrade seed, or by an explicit `sonata auth trust`; in a project config it
  needs the explicit trust. Non-loopback plain http is never bindable. Session
  and OAuth gateways hold no sendable key and are unaffected.
- **`keys.json` is no longer read as empty on a parse error.** Writers refused
  nothing and rewrote the file from what parsed, so one torn write deleted
  every other key (`writeSonataKey`) or unlinked the file (`removeSonataKey`).
  Writers now refuse with a clear error naming the file when it exists but
  cannot be read or parsed, and all writes are atomic (temp file plus rename,
  0600).
- **`sonata auth login` can no longer report success without logging in.**
  The login ran LiteLLM's authenticator against the live token directory,
  which returns a stored — possibly revoked — token as locally unexpired. It
  now runs into a fresh temp directory swapped in only on success, so a
  failed login leaves the working credential untouched. Permission fix-up
  (0700/0600) runs on failure paths too.
- **Withholding a key is per tenant, not machine-wide.** One routed request
  from a cloned repo whose `base_url` host was unbound used to 502 that gateway
  for every project. Each project's own gateways are checked now: only the
  project whose host is unbound loses that gateway (its LiteLLM models and its
  direct requests), and a project that binds the same name keeps its key.
- **Unbound-host messages name the config that set the URL.** The 502 and
  `sonata doctor` say to remove a URL you did not choose rather than trust it,
  and to run `sonata auth trust <gateway> <host>` only if you chose it. Doctor
  checks every routed config, not only the one in the current directory.
- **`sonata auth add` binds nothing from a config.** It read the gateway URL
  off the config in effect, which a cloned repo can carry, so `auth add` could
  trust a repo's host for good. It now reports the unbound host, the config
  that set it, and the trust command. `sonata init` binds only the URLs typed
  in its own run, never one read from an existing config.
- **`[auto_route]` sends a stored decision key only to a bound host.** A
  project's `base_url` received the decision key with no host check. TypeSafe
  and OpenRouter are bound by name; a custom host with a stored key needs
  `sonata auth trust auto-route <host>`, or a URL typed in `sonata init`; the
  machine config's own `[auto_route]` URL is trusted like its gateways. A
  keyless local decision server needs no trust. For a keyed unbound host the
  decision is skipped, the task text is not sent, the tier falls back, and the
  reason is logged and recorded. Decision fetches refuse redirects.
- **`sonata init` does not refresh a model list from an unbound host.** The
  wizard sent each stored key to its URL's host to list models. It now checks
  first: an unbound host is not asked, the harness list stands, and the reason
  is shown. A URL typed in the same run counts as bound.
- **Trust-file writers refuse a corrupt file.** `addTrustBinding` read the file
  tolerantly, so one corrupt `trusted-hosts.json` was wiped by the next `trust`,
  and every confirmed binding with it. Writers now refuse, naming the file, and
  the read-modify-write of the trust file and of `keys.json` runs under the
  existing session lock, so concurrent `auth add`, `auth trust` and `init` runs
  cannot drop each other's changes.
- **Upstream requests refuse redirects.** A gateway's 3xx would have carried the
  key and the conversation to whatever host it named. Upstream fetches now fail
  on a redirect instead of following it.
- **Host bindings compare the port.** A host bound on one port was bound on
  every port. A non-default port is part of the host now; the https default
  port is the same as none.
- **Upgrade: existing configs are trusted once, and only the ones that predate the upgrade.**
  On the first run after upgrading, `sonata serve`, `sonata doctor`, `sonata auth
  add` and `sonata init` bind, once, the host of every https (or loopback http)
  api-key gateway that has a stored or opencode-sourced key, in the machine config
  and in each project a session recorded before the install ran in whose
  `sonata.toml` was last changed before the install (the later of its mtime and
  change time). Residual: a config brought into a project that was already in use
  before the upgrade is seeded too, if it was in place before the install. The install time is the change
  time of the package's manifest. A project opened or cloned after the upgrade is
  never seeded, and neither is the directory a command happens to run in. Each
  binding is reported by `sonata serve` and `sonata doctor`, and
  `sonata auth untrust <gateway> <host>` removes one. A marker in
  `trusted-hosts.json` is written on the first post-upgrade run whether or not any
  key is stored, so the seed runs once; a fresh install seeds nothing. The gateway
  name `seeded` is reserved for the marker.
- **`sonata auth login` leftover backups are swept.** A login that crashed while
  swapping in its new credential left the previous one beside it; a later
  successful login now removes such a backup once it is ten minutes old, so a
  login in progress keeps its rollback copy. The swap is brief: for the moment
  between the two renames the previous credential sits in a `.login-*-old`
  backup beside the live one, and a crash in that window leaves it there until
  the next successful login.

- **A base URL is accepted only in its plain form, and only its href is sent.**
  Node's `URL` and httpx (LiteLLM's client) disagree on the authority of
  `https://openrouter.ai\@evil.example/api/v1`: Node reads `openrouter.ai`,
  httpx reads `evil.example`, so a repo could pass the well-known check while its
  key went elsewhere. A gateway or `[auto_route]` `base_url` now parses only as
  scheme, host, optional port and path, with no userinfo, backslash, whitespace,
  control character, query, fragment or percent-encoded authority, and it is
  stored as its `URL` href. The probe is recorded in the code.
- **A gateway name cannot be an Object.prototype property, and `seeded` is
  refused.** A name such as `constructor` read an inherited value from the plain
  maps keyed by name, which could make the seed throw and abort `auth add` and
  `init`. A gateway name that is empty, has a control character, or is an
  Object.prototype name is refused. The name lookups in the config parser, the
  provider and LiteLLM tables, plan detection, the key stores and the trust file
  read own properties only.
- **Doctor never lists decision models at an unbound host with its stored key.**
- **A decision and the send that follows it use one config.** The unbound-host check
  for a tenant is computed from the config the request carries, for both the LiteLLM
  config and the direct path, rather than from the last build.
- **TypeSafe and OpenRouter decision hosts match with their port.** A port other
  than the default is a different server and gets no well-known key.
- **Unbound-URL messages lead with the remove instruction.** "If you did not choose
  this URL, remove it from <file>" comes first, then the trust command.
- **The init refresh's binding check is required, not optional.**
- **A rollback copy of a login is aged from when it was set aside, and a failed
  rollback names where the previous credential is.** A crashed login's staging
  directory is swept once a day old.
- **Residual: LiteLLM's own client follows redirects.** Sonata's fetches refuse
  them, but a gateway served through LiteLLM can answer with a redirect that
  LiteLLM follows. LiteLLM strips `Authorization` on a cross-host redirect but not
  `x-api-key` or `x-goog-api-key`, so a key sent under those headers can reach the
  redirect's host. Use a gateway that does not redirect, or serve it directly.

### Fixed

- **Generated `-auto` guidance keeps the exhausted-route recovery.** When an
  `-auto` dispatch fails with "all native routes … failed", the agent now re-runs
  that dispatch on the tier the error names (or `-normal`) and keeps later
  dispatches on `-auto`, matching `sonata-loop`. Run `sonata init` to refresh the
  block.
- **A `sonata init` blocked by an unreadable config now exits non-zero.** The
  interactive wizard printed the refusal and exited 0.
- **`route auto` no longer leaves routing on after a settle.** A subagent that
  started and stopped inside the settle slack interval kept the routing env for
  good; a completed settle is now recorded and no longer counts as settling.
- **A watchdog whose wrapper was killed now terminates the surviving harness**
  instead of exiting and leaving it with no timeout.
- **A permission mode that is not a string in a session file is refused** instead
  of being coerced to an alias.
- **`sonata restart` no longer joins a router it did not start** after the grace
  period, and a lazy LiteLLM child that exited before becoming ready is no longer
  terminated a second time (about 10 s of extra wait).
- **The dashboard says "1 turn"** for a single withdrawn turn.

- **An idle `sonata` TUI no longer grows to gigabytes.** A shell left open for
  6.5 h reached 1.2 GB RSS at ~14% idle CPU. The usage screen re-read and
  re-parsed the whole 7-day ledger every 5 s (~215 ms CPU, ~30 MB of fresh
  allocations per poll on a 23 MB ledger) and the status screen did the same
  every 2 s. Both now use an incremental ledger reader (`createLedgerReader`):
  per day file it keeps the parsed rows and the byte offset consumed, parses
  only newly appended complete lines, reparses a file that shrank or was
  replaced, drops files that left the window, and returns the same array while
  nothing changed so the usage report is not re-aggregated either. The models.dev
  cache age is read from a stat-keyed cache instead of re-parsing a 1.7 MB file
  each poll. Windowing is exact on the row timestamp, as before; budget, doctor
  and the CLI keep `readRows`.
- **The init wizard no longer re-parses the models.dev and Artificial Analysis
  caches on every keypress.** They were loaded in the render body; they are now
  loaded through a file-identity cache (path, size, mtime), so the object is
  stable between renders (which lets the family cache hit) and a mid-wizard
  refresh that rewrites the file is still seen.
- **The TUI clocks re-render only when the text changes.** The status and usage
  screens ticked state every second for an "updated Ns ago" label; they now
  skip the render when the label is unchanged.
- **A run's timeout watchdog no longer outlives its wrapper.** If the tmux
  session was killed, the watchdog's single `sleep <run_timeout_seconds>` kept
  running (ppid 1) for up to the full timeout, which left `sonata-run-*/cmd.sh`
  processes behind after test runs. It now sleeps in one-second steps and exits
  once the wrapper is gone.

- **Codex (ChatGPT) prompt cache now hits across a conversation's turns.**
  The router sent LiteLLM no session id, so its chatgpt provider invented a
  new random `session_id` per request and the upstream cache keyed on it
  almost never hit (~15% vs ~99% on other gateways). Each turn was billed as
  an uncached prompt, draining the ChatGPT plan's usage several times
  faster. The router now also sends `x-litellm-session-id` set to the
  per-conversation key (else Claude Code's session id).
- **`sonata init` lists models for every provider you select.** A provider
  picked without typing a key — its key already stored by sonata or held by
  opencode, as Mistral, Google and OpenRouter usually are — has no models in
  any harness's catalogue, and the models step only asked providers that did
  (or whose key was typed this run) what they serve. Their models were missing
  from the picker. Every selected provider with a key is now asked, at its
  well-known URL when no config names one, and the models picked are written
  with that URL.
- **`-free` models are ranked again.** A free route such as OpenCode Zen's
  `kimi-k3-free` or `muse-spark-1.3-contributor-free` carries the same weights
  as its paid name, but Artificial Analysis scores only the paid name, so the
  free one matched nothing and was never ranked. It is now scored as its paid
  equivalent — the way OpenRouter's `:free` already was — unless the catalog
  has a row under the `-free` name itself. A `-contributor-free` model takes
  the derived contributor row, not the standard model's.
- **`sonata init` no longer writes a config that will not load.** Re-running
  init after deselecting every model of an avoided gateway wrote the saved
  `avoid_gateways` entry back verbatim, and `parseConfig` refuses an unknown
  gateway name — so the written file failed to parse. `avoid_gateways` is now
  filtered to gateways the file writes, the same filter `gateway_order`
  already carried. `plan` additionally parses the TOML it is about to write
  and refuses — showing and writing nothing — when the writer emits something
  unloadable, and `apply` re-checks before the first byte hits the disk.
- **`sonata init` no longer silently replaces a config it cannot read.** A
  file that exists but fails to parse — including one stamped with a newer
  `schema_version`, which `applyMigrations` refuses on purpose — used to be
  reported on one line while init rewrote it from defaults, deleting
  `[budget]`, prices and tiers. Init now refuses only when the file at the
  scope being written is unreadable — after the scope is known, so a broken
  project config never blocks a global init and vice versa — names that
  file and the parse error, says to fix the file or move it aside to start
  over, and writes nothing.
- **A price window no longer charges unset rates at $0 while it runs.** A
  window setting only `input` used to replace the flat rates entirely, so
  output and cache reads priced at nothing for the window's duration. Each
  rate a window does not set now falls back to the flat rate.
- **A hand-written `[price]` without `cached_input` no longer charges cache
  reads at $0.** Cache reads fall back to the `input` rate, erring toward
  overcounting rather than undercounting. Scraped models.dev tables still
  decline a partial rate instead of filling the gap.
- **Non-streamed (`stream: false`) 200s no longer record 0 tokens.** The
  usage recorder parsed a streamed body only with the SSE collector, so a
  JSON 200 escaped pricing and `[budget]`. It now accumulates an
  `application/json` body, bounded like the other collectors, and reads
  usage from the finished document with the existing JSON reader.
- **`sonata approve` is no longer allow-listed, so approvals reach a human.**
  `Bash(sonata approve:*)` sat on the auto-allow list alongside `dispatch` and
  `wait`, so a dispatched model could answer a codex or reasonix approval card
  itself with no prompt. Only `dispatch` and `wait` stay allow-listed; every
  `sonata approve` call now goes through Claude Code's permission prompt. The
  generated wrapper text says the main thread runs approve itself, `sonata
  init` removes a stale approve entry when it next rewrites the settings, and
  `sonata doctor` flags it until then.
- **Claude Code's `dontAsk` mode no longer dispatches as `default`.**
  An unrecognised mode used to fall back to `default` silently, and `dontAsk`
  (auto-deny anything not allow-listed) landed there — handing codex
  workspace-write, the most permissive end for the most restrictive session
  mode. `dontAsk` now maps to `plan` (read-only; every adapter already honours
  it without writing, and write roles under it refuse where a harness cannot
  honour it), and any other unknown mode refuses with a named error rather
  than guessing. The capture hook passes the raw value through unchanged.
- **A dispatch cut off by the caller's tool timeout no longer loses its run
  id.** `dispatch_window_seconds` defaulted to 1500 s while Claude Code's Bash
  tool caps at 600 s, and the id was printed only after the blocking wait
  returned — so a killed caller never learned the id. `sonata dispatch` now
  prints `dispatched <id> model=<m>` as each candidate launches, before
  blocking; the default window drops to 540 s; the generated wrapper text tells
  the agent to pass `timeout: 600000` and to resume a cut-off call with
  `sonata wait <id>`.
- **Quit-watcher subshells in the codex and reasonix launch scripts no longer
  loop past the run they watch.** Both waited on `report.md` alone, so a run
  whose harness exited without a report leaked the watcher forever. Each now
  also stops when the `exit` sentinel exists, and reasonix no longer types the
  task when its 60 s readiness loop falls through without the composer — the
  run is already over then, and typing blind lands text into whatever the pane
  holds.

- **Two sessions starting together no longer leave the second unrouted.**
  With the router down, both SessionStart hooks spawned a daemon; one won
  the port and the other exited with EADDRINUSE, then polled only for its
  own instance id until the deadline ran out. Once its spawned child has
  exited — or after a short grace period — the loser now joins any healthy
  multi-tenant sonata router already answering the port, instead of waiting
  out the full 60 s. A non-sonata listener, or a pre-multi-tenant router,
  is still never joined. The join is reported as `joined` rather than with
  the loser's pid and log, and `sonata restart` never joins: a stop that
  failed to free the port is an error, not a restart.
- **The last SubagentStop no longer strips the routing env during another
  session's settle window.** The stop removed the env unconditionally,
  un-routing a session that had written it but might not have read it yet.
  It now checks the session registry first and leaves the env in place for
  that session's own settle to remove. The registry stores a registration
  time per session, so a session that settled long ago but is still live no
  longer holds the env open; registry writes are atomic (tmp file plus
  rename) so lock-free readers never see a half-written file.
- **A failed lazy LiteLLM start no longer orphans a SIGTERM-deaf child.**
  The lazy path sent SIGTERM alone and forgot the pid, so a child stuck in
  a device-code login survived as an orphan. It now escalates to SIGKILL
  after a bounded wait and waits once more after SIGKILL before the retry
  spawns — the same sequence the eager-failure path and `stop()` use —
  keeps the pid recorded until the exit is seen, and no longer spawns while
  a stop is in flight.
- **Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor no longer refuses every Claude Code request.**
  Its server rejects a tool schema whose pattern uses the `\0` (NUL) escape,
  and Claude Code sends every tool on every request, so it failed them all.
  The router now writes that escape as `\x00` — the same character — before
  sending.
- **Strict tool-schema validators no longer refuse every request.** Claude
  Code sends every tool — its own and every MCP server's — on every request,
  so one schema a model's validator rejects fails them all. On the LiteLLM
  path the router now rewrites only the tools that would be refused, each
  case measured against Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor or reported against a real
  MCP server:
  - a schema nested more than 10 levels deep, counting `$ref`s inlined, is
    cut to 10, keeping each cut parameter's type and description (shared
    definitions stay shared, so the tool does not grow);
  - a recursive schema — including a recursive definition nothing uses, and
    `$ref: "#"` — is unrolled to that depth;
  - each `pattern` is rewritten into the regex subset JavaScript, Python and
    RE2 all accept (an unescaped `[` inside a class is escaped, a named group
    becomes plain, an over-1000 repeat bound is opened), or dropped where only
    a lookaround or backreference would do.

  Every other tool is sent unchanged. A model that still refuses a tool schema
  is skipped for the next candidate instead of ending the request.
- **A tool call a model writes as text that cannot be recovered no longer
  ends the agent.** On tier routes, which carry only subagent traffic, the
  router holds a response until its first real tool call or its end, so a
  turn carrying an unrecoverable call is withdrawn and the next ranked model
  asked, as for a 5xx — once per request; later models stream as before. A
  turn that calls tools properly streams from that call on; one that only
  thinks and writes text reaches the client when it ends (at most 5 minutes
  held, then it streams). A main session and bare `--model` requests are
  never held. Only a `<tool_call>` tag followed by a call body (`<function=…>` or
  `{`) counts: the tag merely mentioned in prose is ordinary text, and a call
  quoted in a code fence or backticks is never recovered into a real one.
  Text already sent before a call still reaches the client, as before; when
  no other model serves, the withdrawn turn is served after all. A withdrawn
  turn was still billed, so it gets a ledger row of its own, marked
  `withdrawn`: priced and counted toward `[budget]`, and shown by `sonata
  usage`, the usage screen and the web UI beside the totals rather than as a
  served request. A model that does this twice within 30 minutes is skipped
  for 30 minutes instead of 60 seconds, and `sonata doctor` names it with the
  reason.

### Changed

- **`sonata usage` says when requests used an explicit tier while
  auto-routing is on** — one line, shown only when there were any. Explicit
  tiers remain a legitimate manual override.
- **Orchestrators are told to report `-auto` trouble, not route around it.**
  The loop skill, the managed CLAUDE.md block and the generated `-auto`
  agents now say that a manual override means the user asked for a tier,
  that a misbehaving `-auto` dispatch is retried on `-auto` and reported, and
  that review-failure escalation applies only to the task that failed.

## [0.16.5] - 2026-10-15

### Added

- **Contributor models are ranked.** A `-contributor` model (Muse Spark 1.3
  Contributor, Gemini 4 Argon Contributor on OpenCode Go) is the standard
  model on other terms — your prompts may be used for training — at another
  price. Artificial Analysis scores only the standard model, so `sonata init`
  never offered the contributor. It now takes the standard model's scores
  and rescales its cost per task by the price difference, and labels it in
  the ranking so the trade-off is your choice.
- **Models served only on Google's protocol work.** OpenCode Go serves its
  Gemini models (Gemini 4 Argon Contributor) only on Google's own
  `generateContent` API. A new `api = "google"` on the model routes it there;
  `sonata init` writes it from models.dev, and `sonata doctor` names a model
  missing it. That protocol exists only at OpenCode Go's
  `https://opencode.ai/inference/go/v1`, so init now writes that URL instead
  of the older `…/zen/go/v1`, and doctor tells an existing config to switch.

### Fixed

- **`sonata doctor` shows each `[budget] daily_usd` cap** with today's priced
  spend against it, and fails one that is spent. A cap used to be invisible
  until it refused a request.
- **`sonata runs` marks a run that changed nothing** (`unchanged`), the same
  finding its report already carried as `[no worktree change: …]`.

- **`sonata init` can set up a coding or token plan from opencode.** The Z.ai
  and Zhipu GLM Coding Plans, Kimi For Coding, Alibaba's Coding and Token
  Plans, Volcengine Ark, Tencent, Xiaomi, StepFun and KUAE Cloud plans had no
  known base URL, so an opencode login to one could not be used with a key.
  Each now has one, and is reported as a subscription.

- **Codex models no longer go down every time codex refreshes its login.**
  Refreshing a ChatGPT login revokes the copy the router's LiteLLM was
  using, and every ChatGPT model answered 502 until `sonata restart`. The
  router now notices the refusal — including the backend's own 401 — and,
  when codex holds a newer login, restarts LiteLLM with it by itself. It asks
  for `codex login` only when there is no newer login to take.
- **`sonata doctor` reports a ChatGPT login the router cannot use** as a
  failing `serve gateways` check. It used to say ok while every codex model
  was refused.
- **OpenCode Go's GPT models work.** OpenCode Go serves `gpt-6-luna` and
  `gpt-5.6-luna` only on the Responses API and refused every request sonata
  sent them over chat completions — often ending the request instead of
  trying the next model. `sonata init` now writes `api = "responses"` for any
  model models.dev says needs it, `sonata doctor` names one that lacks it,
  and the router falls straight through past the refusal. Existing configs:
  run `sonata catalog update`, then `sonata doctor`, and add the line it names
  (or re-run `sonata init`).

- **`sonata usage` no longer runs a covered amount into the token column.**
  A bucket whose work was all covered shows `$128.26 sub`, which filled the
  spend column exactly and left no gap (`63M / 196k$128.26 sub`). The column
  is wider and every cell keeps its leading space.

## [0.16.4] - 2026-10-14

### Fixed

- **Flat-rate plans are reported as subscriptions, not per-token spend.**
  OpenCode Go was priced like pay-as-you-go: its work counted toward
  `[budget]` and `sonata usage` showed it as billed, though it is a monthly
  plan. Every key-authenticated plan with an endpoint of its own is now
  recognised from the gateway's `base_url` — OpenCode Go, the Z.ai and Zhipu
  GLM Coding Plans, Kimi For Coding, Alibaba's Coding and Token Plans,
  Volcengine Ark, Tencent, Xiaomi and StepFun plans, KUAE Cloud — and
  reported as covered: valued at list price, left out of `[budget]`. The
  same vendors' metered endpoints are unchanged. The list follows
  models.dev's provider catalogue, which opencode also reads. Rows already
  in the ledger keep the label they were written with.
- **A restart no longer fails a whole tier.** When `sonata restart` killed
  LiteLLM under an in-flight request, the router tried every remaining
  model against the dead process and recorded each as failed — eleven in one
  measured tier. A refused connection to LiteLLM now stops the LiteLLM-backed
  candidates at once (a model on a direct gateway is still tried) without
  recording or cooling any of them, and the tier's 529 says LiteLLM is not
  answering — still naming `sonata dispatch`, which works without it.

### Added

- **`billing = "subscription" | "metered"` on a gateway.** For a plan that
  shares its pay-as-you-go endpoint, where only the key says which it is —
  MiniMax Token Plan, Synthetic, Chutes, NanoGPT, Ollama Cloud, Cerebras Code
  — or to correct sonata either way. `sonata doctor` lists every gateway it
  counts as a subscription and why, and names a gateway on a shared endpoint
  that has not said. For a plan endpoint `sonata init` proposes the plan's
  pay-as-you-go sibling as its `pricing_provider`, since models.dev lists
  plans at $0, and a $0 rate is no longer taken as a covered row's list price.

### Security

- **Dependency and code-scanning fixes.** `smol-toml` (the TOML parser) is
  locked at 1.9.1, past a quadratic-time parse on long documents; the
  development-only `source-map-js` at 1.2.2. The release script treats a
  version as literal text when it looks up its changelog section (it had
  escaped only `.`, and `--notes` takes a tag name from CI), and the CI
  workflow now runs with a read-only token. Installs from npm already resolved
  the patched `smol-toml`; only the repository's lockfile was behind.

## [0.16.3] - 2026-10-13

### Added

- **`r` on the ranking board resets a tier to the suggested order.** A saved
  ranking is never re-proposed, so a ranking rule that changed in an upgrade
  (like 0.16.2's `complex` near-tie margin) could only be adopted with
  `sonata init --repropose-tiers`, outside the TUI. In `sonata agents`, `r`
  now replaces the list being edited with the order the catalog proposes now;
  nothing is written until you confirm, and `←` discards it. `sonata doctor`'s
  tier-freshness advice names it, and computes its suggestion the same way.

### Fixed

- **An overpriced model reached through two providers is demoted on both.**
  `complex` pushes the costly top end of the price-performance curve to the
  back, but only one route to a given model was marked, so the same model on a
  second gateway could still lead the tier.
- **Deselecting a model on its provider's screen in `sonata init` now
  sticks.** A pick that the Models step showed under another key (a Codex
  model your Codex app also lists) was stored under that key, so going back
  and deselecting it on the Codex screen left it selected.
- **The Models step says when a pick is kept but unranked.** A model chosen
  on a provider's own screen that the ranking catalog cannot cost was listed
  as "not offered", though it is still written to the config. It now has its
  own line saying so.

## [0.16.2] - 2026-10-13

### Changed

- **`complex` no longer pays a large premium for a small capability edge.**
  It ranks by capability and lets cost decide only a near-tie, and "near" was
  1 point. Measured: Claude Opus 5.5 led at `max` (intelligence 57.6,
  $5.98/task) over its own `xhigh` (56.0, $3.46/task) — 73% more per task for
  1.6 points. `complex` now treats any model less than 3 points below the
  strongest as tied with it, so the cheaper one (`xhigh`) leads; a model more than 3 points
  stronger still leads however the prices compare. A model below the
  price-performance knee still follows those at or above it. `simple` and
  `normal` are unchanged. Existing configs keep their saved order until `sonata init --repropose-tiers` (or re-ranking in
  `sonata agents`).

### Fixed

- **Claude (and OAuth) models picked during `sonata init` now reach the Models
  step.** Adding `claude` (your Claude Code account) on the providers screen,
  choosing its models and pressing Continue skipped the Models step, or showed
  it without them. The step listed only models known at startup plus what
  providers' `/models` endpoints returned, and a session or OAuth provider
  added this run is in neither. The picks were kept in state but never drawn,
  so they looked discarded. They now appear, checked, and unchecking one there
  drops it.

## [0.16.1] - 2026-10-12

### Changed

- **Generated agents and the CLAUDE.md block point at `sonata route auto`.**
  A tier agent's description and the `model_not_found` advice in the managed
  CLAUDE.md block named `sonata code` first and `sonata route on` second; they
  now name `sonata route auto` followed by a new `claude` session as the fix, with
  `sonata code` as the one-off alternative. Run `sonata sync` to refresh
  existing agent files.

- **Documentation, ready for public beta.** The user guide is published as a
  site on GitHub Pages (`docs/`, built with VitePress by a new `docs`
  workflow). The README is now the front door — status, quickstart, how it
  works — with the full `sonata init` walkthrough moved to a new *Getting
  started* page and every command and flag to a new *Commands* page (adding
  `sonata wait`, `sonata tui`, `usage --by route`/`--project` and
  `status --global`, which the old table missed). Every guide page was checked
  against the source: Claude models are no longer described as filtered out,
  tier ordering and the `<role>-auto` agents are described as they work, and
  the configuration reference now covers `schema_version`, `avoid_gateways`,
  `gateway_order`, `[budget]`, `[native.ports]`, every gateway and model key,
  and `credential_source`. New `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `SECURITY.md`.

## [0.16.0] - 2026-10-12

### Added

- **Claude models are ordinary models.** A tier may rank Claude ids that a
  gateway serves (Copilot, OpenRouter, any other) and, through a new
  `auth = "session"` gateway, models on your own Claude Code account — the
  router forwards the session's credential, only ever to `api.anthropic.com`.
  `sonata init` offers both. Every request is priced at its API list rate:
  subscription work (`codex-oauth`, `copilot-oauth`, and a Claude
  subscription session) shows as `$x sub` in `sonata usage`, `sonata status`
  and the loop panel, and still never counts toward `[budget]`.

- **The sonata-loop skill is now also a Claude Code mod with a live panel.**
  One line per task and per tier agent: state, the model the router served
  (`≈` and `unknown` where it cannot be attributed, never `$0`), tokens,
  elapsed time, and what a running agent is doing and how recently; an agent
  silent for 90 s reads `stalled`. Selecting a row opens its token breakdown
  (input, output, cache read, cache write) and its applied diff beneath it.
  The orchestrator reports the plan through the mod's `sonata_loop` tool;
